recipes.name: Easy Vegetable Pot Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of potato soup
2 (9 inch) frozen prepared pie crusts, thawed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a medium bowl, combine potato soup, mixed vegetables, milk, thyme, and black pepper.
Spoon filling into bottom pie crust. Cover with top crust, and crimp edges to seal. Slit top crust, and brush with beaten egg if desired.
Bake for 40 minutes. Remove from oven, and cool for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Vegetable Pot Pie
raw_recipe.description: Pull what you need from the freezer or pantry from this one. Frozen pie crust, a can of cream of potato soup, and a mega can of mixed veggies. An egg, some milk and a dash of thyme, and you have the fixings for a wonderful pie that your family will think

review.reviewBody: This is the best vegetable pot pie! I did what someone else said and baked the bottom crust a little first. I also added some Lawry's seasoned salt and a touch of cayenne pepper.. I like hot food. Also I didn't have potatoe soup and used mushroom just as good, plus added a little can of chopped mushrooms to the vegetable mis.I got such great reviews... I am actually making another right now! It is so easy and taste so good!

I have made this pie twice. I made a few modifications on the second one. I used frozen mixed veggies, cooked for 5 minutes in the microwave, drained, and cooled. I sauteed some onion in butter to add. I cut the black pepper in half, as I found 1/2 is way too much. I added only a dash of thyme and a little Jane's Crazy Salt to taste. I did not pre-bake 
 the bottom crust or use the egg on the top one. I had to bake the pie 20 minutes longer than the recipe called for because it was not browning. I turned the oven to 400 degrees for the last 20 minutes. It turned out delicious. Hearty and filling.

I was sort of doing my own thing and then came here to see what people did for oven time. 
I added salt, pepper, parsley and garlic powder to the crust. 
Sautéed some Vidalia onion, celery and 3 cloves of garlic. Added the drained mixed veggies and condensed soup and heated everything up. Skipped the milk. 
Baked 450 for 15 minutes, and turned it down to 350 for about 40 more. Beautiful.

Good pie! Added chicken, salt, and used cream of chicken instead)gluten free). Added a splash of almond milk. Also used philo dough for crusts as I needed a gluten free option. Just thawed and rolled out to fit pie plate.

Quick, easy, and delicious. Perfect for a cold fall/winter night. This is now on our weekly/biweekly dinner rotation. Has a real homemade taste and aroma, which is nice after a hard work day.
I use Pillsbury refrigerated pie crusts (which we buy, freeze, and thaw) and Campbell's cream of potato soup. I play with the canned vegetables. Right now, Del Monte Vegetable and Bean Blends- California Style is a hit (note that it has white kidney beans in it- which work). I agree with other reviewers: bake the bottom pie crust a little first- I do just a few minutes- until it's starting too brown- not too much).
Highly recommended for people who want something warm and cozy (without meat) and don't really have loads of time to spend cooking (or even if you do!). Thanks for this great recipe!

I didn't have cream of potato soup so used cream of celery & chopped up a potato. Since thyme can be strong & to make the texture better we used ground thyme at around 1/8 tsp which was just right. You could use thyme leaf also. I only put the crust on the top as I only had 1 on hand. Will make again & may try adding chicken & mushrooms while trying as others suggested herb de prov.

I made a few changes based on other reviews. I used 1/2 cup each of frozen green beans, peas and corn along with fresh diced carrots and potatoes. Instead of cream of potato soup and used cream of celery. My spices were 1/4 tsp of thyme, rosemary, salt and pepper. I pre-baked my bottom crust and put all in a deep dish. My husband loved it and I will definitely make again.

Really good! Made my own potato soup with celery, onion, potato, chicken boullion, water, milk...cooked down to a mashed concentrated state, quite thick. Seasoned. Added the veggies. Loved the thyme in it. Cool before transferring mixture to pie shell. No egg wash. Thanks :)

Just made this and it turned out great. I used a deep dish so doubled the recipe and it worked great. Pre-baked the crust for about 11 minute and then added the filling and top crust. Also added broccoli florets with the mixed vegetables for a better veggie. Will definitely make this again.

Pie was very good. A few changes: used 3-inch deep 7x7-inch casserole dish. Did not bake bottom crust as intended, yet it was not mushy. Due to depth of dish, baked pie 1 hour. Bottom crust did not touch top edge of dish, which was good. Added mixture, top crust, and fluted edge. Covered edge with aluminum foil to prevent burning, baking 40 minutes. Uncovered edge, baked additional 20 minutes. Used ingredients on hand (12 oz bag of frozen mixed veggies + 1 handful frozen corn, cream of mushroom soup, refrigerated prepared pie crusts - kept on counter 10 minutes, as pkg directed, before rolling out). Didn't use thyme or black pepper nor did I brush top crust with egg. Pie was beautiful at end of bake; very pleased with results. Enjoyed making this - thanks for sharing.

My daughter has been asking for a meatless pot pie since she became a pescatarian. I found this recipe and although I made tweaks, it was a hit! I used cream of mushroom instead of cream of potato. I also sautéed onions, garlic cloves & fresh diced veggies: potatoes, carrots, celery, frozen broccoli & frozen peas. I also used the thyme, pepper & andded: onion and garlic powder (I would have used rosemary, if I didn’t run out).
Quick and easy. Family loved it.
Sometimes I use soup mix in place of the canned vegetables. They require a little precook step if they are frozen mix.

Great simple recipe. I added a bit of idahoan potato powder to thicken the filling up a little before putting it in the oven. I can see adjusting this recipe in the future with little tweaks, like adding shredded chicken breast, etc to suit what I'm in the mood for! Thanks for sharing!!

Ok this was easy and really yummy. However, just because it has the word "veggie" in the title doesn't make it vegetarian. The one ingredient you need to watch for is the pie crusts. For a true vegetarian option, you need to check the ingredients of your pie crust to see if it contains lard. I reached out to Pillsbury to inquire if their "lard" is truly lard or made from purely vegetable sources. I haven't heard back yet.
Easy and wasvreally good. I used frozen vegetables. I should have doubled the recipe though to fill the pot pie.
This was not good nor bad; a little peppery for my liking and I miss the chicken and cheese that my recipe has so I'll just stick with it. However, this recipe would be great for vegatarians.
